summary:
Project Nevada is an interactive, SI-powered SCADA dashboard designed for the "Flame in Freefall" challenge to summarize, rank and interpret microgravity combusion experiments from NASA's Physical Sciences Information (PSI) reposity. While NASA has collected decades of ISS fire data, the volume and complexity of raw results make them difficult to compare or apply to variable-gravity habitats.

Our platform organizes ket PSI datasets across Prevention (BASS, BASS-II, Saffire I-III, ACME BRE, CFI-G), Detection (SAME, SAME-R, DAFT, DAFT-2) and Suppression (Flex CO2/Helium dilution, ISS Fine Water Mist). Using TOPSIS multi-criteria ranking and partial-gravity physics bounding between 0g(ISS) and 1g(Earth) alongside E-FIELD ion-wind data, users can evaluate habita-specific risks, predict material flammablity limits and explore Earth firefighting spin-offs. This makes lunar and Martian exploration safer, especially where elevated oxygen levels (>=30% O2 at <=  10.2 psi) increase fire hazards.
details:
1. WHAT PROJECT NEVADA DOES & HOW IT WORKS
Project Nevada is a minimalist, SI-powered SCADA Human-Machine Interface (HMI) built for the "Flame in Freefall" challenge. It transforms raw, complex microgravity combustion records from NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository into an interactive, three-column engineering dashboard designed for aerospace engineers, researchers, professors, and students:

• Column 1 — Habitat Controls & NASA’s Three Fire Safety Pillars: Users select target crew environments—ISS (14.7 psi, 21% O2, 0g), EVA Spacesuits (4.3 psi, 100% O2), Lunar Base & Pressurized Rovers (<=10.2 psi, >=30–34% O2, 0.16g), or Mars Habitats (0.38g)—and adjust Oxygen concentration (%) and Gravity (g). Three primary actuator controls map directly to NASA's core fire-safety architecture:
- LED (Prevention): Material flammability limits & quiescent HVAC fan cutoff (BASS/BRE).
- BUZZER (Detection): Smoke aerosol vs. planetary regolith dust discrimination (SAME/DAFT-2).
- RELAY (Suppression): CO2/Helium dilution & ISS Fine Water Mist activation (FLEX).

• Column 2 — Real-Time Status & TOPSIS Relevance Ranking: Displays live chamber telemetry, flame morphology (contrasting spherical diffusion flames in 0g against buoyant plumes in partial gravity), and dynamically ranks core PSI investigations (0–100 score) using Euclidean TOPSIS multi-criteria decision analysis tailored to the chosen habitat.

• Column 3 — Partial-Gravity Flammability Prediction & Reference Metrics: Visualizes flame spread velocity (Vf in mm/s) across variable gravity (0g to 1g) and Minimum Oxygen Concentration (MOC %) self-extinction boundaries.

2. BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT (SPACE & EARTH)
• Safer Space Exploration: Enables rapid comparison of material flammability limits, preventing spacecraft disasters like Apollo 1 (1967), Apollo 13 (1970), the 1997 Mir oxygen-generator fire, and recent alarm events such as Artemis II. It specifically addresses the Lunar pre-breathe paradox, where intermediate atmospheres (>=30% O2 at <=10.2 psi—over 40% higher O2 than Earth) significantly heighten fire risks.


• Earth Firefighting Spin-Offs: Highlights how NASA PSI technologies transfer directly to Earth safety—including ISS Fine Water Mist extinguishers (<100-micron droplets that suppress fires without damaging electronics in server rooms), Shuttle/SAME/DAFT-2 dust-immune smoke detectors for mining safety, and lighter carbon-wrapped SCBA breathing tanks and thermal turnout gear for terrestrial firefighters.

3. HOW OUR PROJECT IS CREATIVE

Instead of building a static data catalog, Team Nevada reimagined NASA PSI analytics as an industrial SCADA control panel paired with a Partial-Gravity Bounding Engine. Because PSI currently lacks true partial-gravity combustion runs (awaiting future missions such as LUCI and FM2), our engine uses 0g (ISS) and 1g (Earth) empirical results as lower and upper bounds alongside ACME E-FIELD ion-wind data to interpolate the 0.16g Lunar flammability peak in real time.

4. KEY TECHNICAL FACTORS & NASA PSI HARDWARE CONSIDERED

• Hardware Suites & Test Variables: Accounted for shared ISS hardware architectures—including the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) with modular ACME hardware (6 gas-flame studies: BRE, CFI-G up to 85% O2 inverse spherical flames, and E-FIELD Flames), CIR with the Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA for FLEX, FLEX-2, and liquid CFI cool flames), and the Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) with the SPICE modular fan-driven flow duct (BASS, BASS-II, SPICE, SLICE, Saffire I-III, and SAME/DAFT-2).

• Scope Boundary: Explicitly excluded rocket engine propellant combustion from PSI ranking scope, as extreme flow velocities in rocket combustors render combustion nearly gravity-independent.

5. TOOLS, LANGUAGES & SI ACKNOWLEDGMENT

• Tech Stack: Built with TypeScript, React Native Web, Node.js, HTML5/CSS3 SCADA styling, and Python (Matplotlib, python-pptx) for data synthesis and presentation charts.

• Super Intelligence (SI) Disclosure: SI tools (Google Gemini) assisted with code structuring, physics-equation synthesis, and visual mockups; all SI-generated media include explicit metadata and visible "SI-Generated" watermarks without modifying any NASA logos or branding.
